newsitem.title: UK: Look out for lovesick badgers, British drivers told.
newsitem.headline: Look out for lovesick badgers, British drivers told.

text.p: British motorists were warned on Friday to look out for randy badgers likely to throw themselves under the wheels of cars in a frenzied hunt for mates.
The National Federation of Badger Groups (NFBG) said one-fifth of Britain's 250,000 badger population is killed by speeding cars each year.

Most of the deaths happen in the autumn breeding season, when the animals follow ancient badger trails across busy roads in search of a mate. "They cross the roads and are run over by drivers going too fast to stop," said the NFBG's Pauline Kidner.
